instruction: Select all images containing a clock.

game.semantic_variant: Select all things made to tell the time.
game.hint: Select all that apply. If you are unsure, use your best judgement.
game.explanation: Ordinary clocks count, and so does the alarm clock running on legs: impossible, but still a clock. The hourglass in a clock case, the phone hung on the wall showing a clock face and the sundial are borderline cases, recorded without a verdict. The mirror, the decorative plate and the compass are not clocks.

correct: Clocks identified. Your time has been well spent.
Correct. The Department will be on time for once.
partial: Partially correct. A clock is still unaccounted for.
Partially correct. Some clocks ran out of time.
incorrect: Incorrect. The Department has stopped the clock.
Incorrect. Time has been wasted, and recorded.

selection_review.reason: Nine distinct, standardised images reviewed together at tile size: two ordinary clocks (round wall clock with a mint-green rim on a cream wall; dark wooden longcase clock against a white wall), one impossible clock (generated red twin-bell alarm clock running on two legs), three borderline timekeepers (generated hourglass inside a mantel-clock case; generated smartphone hung on a wall showing an analogue dial; photographed bronze sundial on a stone pedestal) and three non-members that share a clock's round, dial-like form (round wall mirror, hand-painted plate on a teal wall, magnetic compass on a tree stump). Views, colours and settings vary within each role; generated images appear among targets and borderline cases alike. The two photographed twin-bell alarm clocks remain in the collection for later versions.
